method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma' (last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed), 43 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma' (four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1), 23 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the hand-written Wave 1 page (which quoted RCH) as a paraphrase. Every Wave 1 claim is carried over and re-anchored in the page as fetched on 2026-09-24. S2 anchors point into a text transcription of the four management flowcharts made in Wave 1; the flowcharts are images and were not re-read, so a person should re-check S2 doses against them before use.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Asthma or anaphylaxis? If you cannot tell, treat as anaphylaxis.** Both need treatment without delay.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Use a metered dose inhaler (MDI) rather than a nebuliser:** it works as well, acts fast and has fewer side effects.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Short-acting beta agonist (SABA) is the core of treatment.** In moderate, severe and life-threatening asthma, start a steroid early.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Adolescents on budesonide/formoterol** (combined reliever-preventer dry powder) who need hospital treatment for a flare get salbutamol instead.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **What it is:** chronic airway inflammation with bronchospasm and obstruction that reverses. In children a viral respiratory infection is the usual trigger, and atopy often coexists.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Under 12 months:** wheeze is probably bronchiolitis, which bronchodilators do not help.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Carbon footprint:** MDIs carry a large one, so dry powder inhalers (DPI) are preferred where they can be used.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Symptoms that start suddenly after a sting, a food or a medicine** point towards anaphylaxis rather than asthma alone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Ask about:** reliever use in this illness (dose, how often, whether it still works) · the preventer (technique, adherence) · triggers such as a cold, passive smoke, exercise, cold air or aero-allergens.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Previous episodes that signal risk:** 2 or more hospital presentations needing treatment · IV treatment · ICU or intubation · SABA used more than twice a week, or more than 3 MDI canisters a year.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Also ask about** symptoms between attacks (night or morning cough, wheeze with exercise), missed school, joining in physical activity, and comorbid anaphylaxis or allergic rhinitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Judge severity by** how the child looks, their mental state and activity, and their work of breathing (rate, accessory muscles, recession).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Unreliable:** how loud the wheeze is, pulsus paradoxus and peak flow. An unwell-looking child whose chest is silent (no wheeze) may be close to respiratory collapse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Supporting but weaker signs:** the first SpO2, the heart rate and whether the child can talk.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tachycardia** may reflect severity, but beta agonists such as salbutamol also cause it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Unequal breath sounds** are common from mucus plugs; if they persist, think of an inhaled foreign body or a pneumothorax.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Red flags for another diagnosis:** productive or isolated cough · paraesthesia · chest pain · clubbing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild:** slightly more work of breathing, normal breathing rate, alert and active. **Moderate:** moderately more work of breathing, faster breathing, still alert and active.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe:** markedly increased work of breathing, fast breathing, agitation, pallor, and any other signs of anaphylaxis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Life-threatening:** maximal work of breathing, fast breathing, confusion or drowsiness, not moving, cyanosis, and any other signs of anaphylaxis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tests are usually unnecessary;** no chest X-ray is needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid routine blood gases:** they distress the child and can tip a child with respiratory compromise into further deterioration. The clinical picture is the better guide.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Check serum potassium** if salbutamol has been used frequently or for a long time.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Standard MDIs:** salbutamol 100 microg per puff; ipratropium bromide 21 microg per puff.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Management is set out as four flowcharts,** one each for mild, moderate, severe and life-threatening asthma (see What the flowcharts say).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **IV magnesium sulfate 50%:** 1 mL contains 2 mmol (500 mg). Dose 0.2 mmol/kg, which is 50 mg/kg or 0.1 mL/kg of the undiluted product, up to 8 mmol. Double-check the dose, dilute to local protocol and check the concentration before giving it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Dexamethasone** has a longer half-life and causes less vomiting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **IM adrenaline in life-threatening asthma** can open the airways when respiratory effort is too poor for inhaled drugs to reach them.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No response to salbutamol?** Get senior advice and look for another cause (e.g. an anatomical airway abnormality, cystic fibrosis, bronchomalacia).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A spacer and mask can go over nasal prong oxygen** to give the inhaled bronchodilator.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Salbutamol toxicity:** tachycardia, tachypnoea and fine tremor. Bloods help confirm it (low potassium, raised lactate, metabolic acidosis) before SABA is paused; the potassium recovers quickly once salbutamol is cut back.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **All severities:** give oxygen by nasal prongs to keep SpO2 at 90% or more; use a nebuliser only if the child cannot manage an MDI.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild, first dose:** 1-5 years, 2-6 puffs of salbutamol MDI through spacer and mask, once; 6 years and over, 12 puffs through a spacer. Reassess after 20 minutes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild, good response** (e.g. less work of breathing): no more salbutamol; reassess 1 hour and 2 hours after the first dose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild, work of breathing not increased at review:** send home with asthma education (check inhaler and spacer technique), an asthma action plan, and follow-up with the usual doctor.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild, some response but little improvement** (work of breathing or oxygen need persisting): manage as moderate; at 6 years and over, give 12 more puffs of salbutamol MDI through a spacer.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild, no response:** get senior advice, stop the salbutamol and think of another diagnosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate:** 1-5 years, salbutamol MDI 6 puffs (spacer and mask) three times, 20 minutes apart, ⚠️ with no steroid; 6 years and over, 12 puffs on the same schedule plus an oral steroid.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oral steroid:** prednisolone 1 mg/kg (up to 50 mg) or dexamethasone 0.3 mg/kg (up to 16 mg); the IV product can be given by mouth.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate, review** 30 minutes after the 3rd salbutamol dose. A good response means better air entry, work of breathing, breathing rate and SpO2.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate, good response:** salbutamol as needed; if it is needed more often than 3 hourly, admit; if 3 hourly or less often, discharge.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate, poor response:** rethink the diagnosis and add ipratropium. 1-5 years: salbutamol 6 puffs every 30-60 minutes as needed with ipratropium bromide 4 puffs, every 20 min × 3 doses, and consider a steroid. 6 years and over: salbutamol 12 puffs every 30-60 minutes as needed with ipratropium 8 puffs, every 20 min × 3 doses. Ipratropium can then continue every 4 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate, still responding poorly:** manage as severe, or admit and keep salbutamol going every 1-2 hours as needed: 6 puffs at 1-5 years, 12 puffs at 6 years and over. On discharge, consider prednisolone 1 mg/kg daily for the next 2 days.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep monitoring** work of breathing, alertness, activity and SpO2. If the child deteriorates: treat as severe, get senior advice, reconsider the diagnosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe:** resuscitation area and senior staff. Every 20 minutes × 3 doses: 1-5 years, salbutamol 6 puffs with ipratropium bromide 4 puffs; 6 years and over, salbutamol 12 puffs with ipratropium 8 puffs (MDI via spacer and mask).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe, systemic steroid:** get IV access and give a corticosteroid early, orally or IV. IV choices: methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg (up to 60 mg) 6 hourly · hydrocortisone 4 mg/kg (up to 100 mg) 6 hourly · dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg (up to 16 mg) every 24-48 hours.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe, second-line IV drugs early** (reassess after each): magnesium sulphate 0.2 mmol/kg (up to 8 mmol) over 20 min; aminophylline 10 mg/kg (up to 500 mg) infused over 30-60 min on a cardiac monitor, repeatable 6 hourly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Life-threatening:** resuscitation area and senior staff; respiratory support with high-flow nasal cannula oxygen, CPAP or bilevel pressure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Continuous nebulised bronchodilators:** salbutamol 2.5 mg nebules with ipratropium bromide 250 microg (younger children), or salbutamol 5 mg with ipratropium 500 microg (older children).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider IM adrenaline** 10 microg/kg (that is 0.01 mL/kg of 1:1000), injected in the lateral thigh; repeat every 5 min as needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Dexamethasone** 0.6 mg/kg IV (up to 16 mg) first, with a further dose after 24-48 hours if needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Aminophylline and magnesium cannot share an IV line;** give them at the same time only through a second cannula.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Not responding:** get paediatric intensive care input. Any child needing maximal asthma treatment belongs in a critical care setting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **IV salbutamol may be considered, though evidence of benefit is limited:** 5-15 microg/kg (up to 300 microg) over 10 min, repeated if needed, or followed by an infusion of 1-2 microg/kg/min (up to 200 microg/min) adjusted to response and heart rate, rising if necessary to 5 microg/kg/min.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Acute asthma', four management flowcharts on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-1-acute-asthma-mild-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-2-acute-asthma-moderate-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-3-acute-asthma-severe-mgmt-flowchart.png ; https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Flowchart-4-acute-asthma-life-threatening-mgmt.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Talk to the local paediatric team** for moderate, severe or life-threatening asthma, a poor response to inhaled salbutamol, or any oxygen need.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Think about transfer** for severe or critical asthma needing IV treatment or respiratory support · a rising oxygen need · poor response to salbutamol or failure to wean it · care beyond what the local hospital is comfortable giving.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge at one hour** is possible for some children, with senior agreement, if all severity signs have gone, activity is normal, parents are skilled and familiar with asthma, and emergency care is close.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Everyone else:** should manage three hours without needing salbutamol MDI, and be eating and drinking adequately.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild hypoxia (SpO2 90-94%) is not a bar to discharge** when the child looks clinically well after a good response to treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Before discharge, check and fill gaps in** recognising and managing symptoms · when to seek help · emergency management · what the reliever and preventer do · inhaler technique.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Arrange follow-up** with the GP or specialist. Update the Asthma Action Plan to cover this episode, and record in the notes that it was given and discussed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider** a community asthma program and education on associated atopic conditions: allergic rhinitis, and ⚠️ anaphylaxis, whose illness and death rates rise when asthma is poorly controlled.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Acute asthma', last updated July 2023, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Asthma_acute/, retrieved 2026-09-24
